lesson.subject: science
lesson.title: Light and Shadows
lesson.summary: Light sources, how we see, shadows and how they change, and staying safe with light and sun.
learning_objectives: Say what a light source is
Explain how we see, with Ibn al-Haytham
Say how shadows change through the day

standards.text: Recognise that we need light to see things and that dark is the absence of light; notice that light is reflected from surfaces; recognise that shadows are formed when light is blocked

success_criteria: I can say how we see things
I can say what makes a shadow
I can say when shadows are long and short
lesson.real_life: Shadow puppets, walking in the sun, and being seen on a bike at night.

blocks.markdown:
Today's big question: how do we see?

We will meet a famous Muslim scientist and play with shadows.
blocks.say: Welcome back, young scientist! Today's big question is: how do we see, and what is a shadow? By the end, you will tell light sources from other things, explain how light helps us see, and make shadows grow and shrink. Let's go!

blocks.alt: Light comes from the Sun, torches and lamps.
blocks.caption: Light comes from the Sun, torches and lamps.

blocks.text: Stop 1: Where does light come from?

blocks.markdown:
A **light source** makes its own light.

The Sun, a torch and a lamp are light sources. The Moon is not.
blocks.say: Light helps us see. Some things make their own light. We call them light sources. The Sun is the biggest light source we know. A torch, a lamp and a candle are light sources too. The Moon is not a light source. It only looks bright because the Sun's light bounces off it. Look at some light sources.

scenes.caption: The Sun is a light source.
scenes.say: The Sun makes its own light. It lights up our whole day.

scenes.caption: A torch and a lamp are light sources.
scenes.say: A torch makes light too. So does a lamp.

scenes.caption: The Moon only reflects light.
scenes.say: The Moon does not make light. It only reflects the Sun's light, so it shines in the sky.

question.prompt: Which of these is a light source?
question.explanation: A torch makes its own light. A book and the Moon do not.

blocks.markdown:
**Ibn al-Haytham** showed that we see when light bounces off things into our eyes.

In the dark, there is no light, so we cannot see.
blocks.say: A long time ago, a Muslim scientist called Ibn al-Haytham worked out how we see. He lived in Basra and Cairo about a thousand years ago. He showed that light travels in straight lines. Light bounces off things and goes into our eyes. That is how we see them. In the dark, there is no light to bounce, so we cannot see.

scenes.caption: Light from a lamp.
scenes.say: A lamp sends out light. It travels in straight lines.

scenes.caption: Light bounces off the ball.
scenes.say: The light hits the ball and bounces off.

scenes.caption: The light goes into the eye.
scenes.say: The light goes into your eye. Now you can see the ball!

question.prompt: We can see things in complete darkness.
question.explanation: We need light to bounce off things into our eyes, so we cannot see in complete darkness.

points: A light source makes its own light
We see when light bounces into our eyes
blocks.say: Let us remember. Light sources make light. Light bounces into our eyes so we can see.

blocks.markdown:
A **shadow** forms when something blocks the light.

The shadow has the same shape as the object.
blocks.say: A shadow is a dark shape. It forms when something blocks the light. Light cannot go through an opaque thing like you, so a dark patch appears behind you. That dark patch is your shadow. A shadow is the same shape as the thing blocking the light. Watch a shadow form.

scenes.caption: The Sun shines on the girl.
scenes.say: The sun shines on a girl. Her body blocks the light.

scenes.caption: The shadow is on the other side.
scenes.say: A dark shadow appears on the ground behind her, on the side away from the Sun.

question.explanation: A shadow forms where an object blocks the light.

blocks.title: Does it make a shadow?
blocks.goal: Opaque things make a shadow. See-through things make a faint shadow. Sort them.
blocks.say: Time to play with shadows! Use a torch and your hands. Move your hand close to the wall and then further away. Which shadow is bigger? Try it, and put the objects into the boxes.

instructions: Switch off the big light and hold the torch pointing at the wall.

points: A shadow forms when something blocks light
Closer to the light makes a bigger shadow
blocks.say: Remember. A shadow is made when something blocks light. Moving the object changes the shadow.

blocks.text: Stop 1: The Sun moves across the sky

blocks.markdown: Shadows are **long** when the Sun is low and **short** when the Sun is high.
blocks.say: The Sun looks as if it moves across the sky from morning to evening. Really it is the Earth turning. This changes our shadows. In the morning the Sun is low, so shadows are long. At midday the Sun is high, so shadows are short. In the evening the Sun is low again, so shadows are long again. Watch a shadow change.

scenes.caption: Morning: a long shadow.
scenes.say: In the morning the Sun is low. The tree has a long shadow.

scenes.caption: Midday: a short shadow.
scenes.say: At midday the Sun is high. The shadow is short, right under the tree.

scenes.caption: Evening: a long shadow again.
scenes.say: In the evening the Sun is low again, on the other side. The shadow is long again.

question.explanation: At midday the Sun is high, so shadows are short.

blocks.say: Time for a brain game. Find the pairs. Then work out when your shadow is the longest.

points: The Sun is low in the morning and evening, so shadows are long
The Sun is high at midday, so shadows are short
blocks.say: Remember. Shadows change length through the day.

blocks.markdown: **Reflective** materials bounce light back, so we can be seen in the dark.
blocks.say: Light keeps us safe. At night, people wear bright or shiny clothes so drivers can see them. Cyclists use lights on their bikes. Street lamps help us see the road. Reflective strips bounce a car's light back so a person shows up in the dark. Look at things that help us be seen.

blocks.alt: A bike light, a bright jacket and a street lamp help us be seen.
blocks.caption: A bike light, a bright jacket and a street lamp help us be seen.
blocks.say: Here are three helpers: a bike light, a bright jacket and a street lamp.

question.prompt: Why do cyclists wear reflective strips at night?
question.explanation: Reflective strips bounce car light back, so drivers can see the cyclist.

blocks.alt: A tree gives shade. Sunglasses and a hat protect us from strong sun.
blocks.caption: A tree gives shade. Sunglasses and a hat protect us from strong sun.
blocks.say: The Sun gives us light but its rays can harm our eyes and skin. Never look straight at the Sun. Wear sunglasses and a hat when it is bright, and stay in the shade at midday. Let's look at the shade made by a tree.

blocks.title: Find the shade
instructions: Go outside on a sunny day.
Find a shadow made by a building or tree. Is it cooler there?
Draw where you would sit to stay safe from strong sun.
blocks.say: Now try this on a sunny day with a grown-up. Find the shade and see how it feels.
